content:
A poll of thousands of 9to5Mac readers has found that price hikes are very likely to extend the upgrade cycle for Apple products, even for the most loyal users.

In the reader responses, "upgrade less often" was by far the most common answer of all the available options, with only 9% of respondents saying that price increases would not affect their purchasing behavior…

As we've noted before, some of the increases have been more than 50%, with memory and storage upgrades doubling in price in some cases—and all signs suggest things aren't likely to improve any time soon.

If anyone would be expected to keep buying Apple products at the same pace despite price hikes, it would be the 9to5Mac readership, but a poll on Friday showed that even this group has its limits.

Over 90% of readers said they would change their purchasing behavior due to the price increases, with more than a third specifically saying they would upgrade less often.

  • Upgrade less often: 38%
  • Wait for sale: 14%
  • Give up one or more Apple products: 12%
  • Buy a lower-tier model: 9%
  • No effect: 9%

Of course, new features could change minds, but it's at least hopeful that Apple will notice the slowdown in sales, and may drop prices somewhat to maintain demand.
